The rapid integration of Artificial Intelligence (AI) models has established a complex supply chain, but many of these shared artifacts harbor severe vulnerabilities such as insecure serialization and architectural backdoors. While prior efforts have extensively scanned model registries to flag malicious artifacts, a critical gap remains in understanding how developers actually adopt and integrate these unsafe models into downstream software systems. We bridge this gap by conducting a large-scale empirical study on the usage and propagation of 16,977 known vulnerable models on HuggingFace flagged by InsightDB. We track their prevalence across GitHub repositories, software packages, fine-tuning chains, and deployed applications. Our analysis reveals that, despite being publicly flagged, these vulnerable models appear in over 21,000 code locations across more than 5,000 open-source repositories, with 3,757 distinct flagged models (22.1\%) actively referenced in at least one project. To understand how these models are integrated in code and identify recurring usage patterns, we categorize and analyze the recurring patterns surrounding them via a customized pipeline that combines Code Property Graphs extraction with a tailored Frequent Subgraph Mining approach. Across all patterns, we find no evidence of provenance verification or model sanitization logic, with developers frequently bypassing security parameters or delegating trust to permissive framework defaults. These findings underscore that scanning model files alone is insufficient, highlighting the urgent need for context-aware security analysis and stricter integration guardrails at the application layer of the AI supply chain.

Purpose This study investigates the impact of pick location height switching on task performance time in manual order picking systems. Drawing on task switching theory, we examine whether switching between ground- and chest-level pick locations increases task performance time, whether switching costs are asymmetric, and whether item weight strengthens possible differences between ground-to-chest and chest-to-ground switches. Design/methodology/approach We adopt a two-stage approach that combines internal validity and operational generalizability. First, a controlled eye-tracking experiment simulates a simplified order picking scenario to explore the cognitive mechanisms underlying visual search when repeating versus switching pick location heights. Second, we analyze 3,537,973 pick location visits from a German grocery retail warehouse to test the effects of pick location height switching in a real-world operational environment with professional order pickers. Findings The eye-tracking experiment provides mechanism-oriented evidence that switching between pick location heights increases visual search time and reorientation demands under controlled conditions. The archival field study complements these behavioral insights by showing that height switching is associated with longer task performance time. It further shows that switching costs depend on direction, with ground-to-chest switches being more time-consuming than chest-to ground switches. This directional difference becomes more pronounced as item weight increases. Practical implications The findings suggest that warehouse managers should consider not only the frequency but also the direction of height switches when designing picking sequences. Batching and routing algorithms could incorporate switching costs as a weighted parameter, with particular attention to ground-to-chest switches involving heavier items. However, reducing height switches should be balanced against ergonomic risks, as long sequences of ground-level picks may increase repetitive bending and musculoskeletal strain. Originality/value This study provides the first empirical evidence on pick location height switching in warehouse operations and extends task switching theory to a new operational context. By combining mechanism-oriented eye-tracking evidence with large-scale field data, we show that height switching is associated with asymmetric switching costs and provide insights into the cognitive and motor reorientation processes that may underlie these effects.

Large language model (LLM) agents are becoming direct users of the open web. As they take on increasingly complex and information-intensive tasks, effective web access is becoming a core capability for agentic problem solving. Existing approaches have advanced agentic web access through different access models, including search-augmented agents, browser-based agents, and, more recently, filesystem-based agents. Nevertheless, as users expect agents to complete long-horizon, end-to-end tasks, they increasingly need to conduct broad information gathering, perform browser actions, and revisit acquired evidence within a single trajectory. Yet our preliminary analyses reveal that existing access models struggle to meet these demands. They primarily support either information gathering or browser interaction, while combining their capabilities can involve substantial costs or performance trade-offs. To this end, we present Web\$hell, an interface that unifies web access under a single access model. Using a common schema defined by WebContract, WebCompiler compiles live webpages into addressable information and action objects. These objects are maintained in WebCache and handled through a shared set of operations, providing agents with consistent, operable, and persistent web access. Through extensive experiments across web search, web navigation, and deep research benchmarks, we show that Web\$hell achieves strong task performance at lower cost. Our results further indicate the importance of interface design for effective web access, with Web\$hell opening new possibilities for more capable and efficient LLM agents on the web.

Digitization in the deep sea port context is often invoked as shorthand for technological modernization, yet its operational meaning and implications vary widely by place. This paper explicates what “digitization” means for the Limbe Deep Sea Port in Cameroon by situating the concept within port operational processes, stakeholder relationships, governance environments, and socioeconomic constraints specific to Limbe and comparable West/Central African ports. Drawing on an interdisciplinary desk-based literature review of academic studies, international agency reports, industry white papers, and regional policy documents, the study adopts a conceptual-analytical approach to define digitization as the systematic conversion and integration of analogue and paper-based port procedures into interoperable digital systems that enable real-time data exchange, automated workflows, evidence-based decision-making, and secure electronic transactions across the port ecosystem. The paper disaggregates digitization into technological (TOS, PCS, VTMS, IoT, analytics, blockchain, cybersecurity), organizational (process re-engineering, governance, procurement), human factors (skills, roles, change management), and regulatory (single window, data governance) dimensions. It identifies measurable indicators to assess progress—transaction digitalization rate, vessel turnaround time, dwell time, customs clearance time, system uptime, and workforce certification rates—and outlines likely benefits (efficiency, transparency, environmental monitoring, regional connectivity) and risks (digital divides, cyber threats, governance bottlenecks, finance constraints). The analysis highlights contextual enablers and barriers for Limbe, including infrastructure, institutional capacity, financing options, and regional integration imperatives. The paper concludes with policy and operational recommendations that prioritize staged interventions—low‑complexity quick wins, mid‑term integration, and long‑term smart-port capabilities—anchored in inclusive governance, blended finance, workforce development, and cyber resilience. The findings aim to provide a clear, practical, and academically grounded definition of digitization tailored to Limbe’s developmental and geopolitical realities. Keywords: Limbe Deep Sea Port; port digitization; Port Community System; Terminal Operating System; Cameroon; smart ports; maritime governance

An AI agent may be authorized to act—but what happens when the real-world result differs from what was authorized? Should that agent still be allowed to continue? As frontier AI models evolve into autonomous systems capable of executing payments, transmitting sensitive information, modifying infrastructure, invoking privileged tools, and controlling physical devices, a fundamental security question emerges: Why should authorization granted before an action remain sufficient when its actual consequences have not yet been independently verified? This paper proposes a different model of machine authority: “Computation is not authority to act. Authority must be earned from the real execution path, not granted indefinitely per session.” The research introduces Receipt-Gated Interim Effectuation Validation (IEV), an execution-control architecture in which a consequential operation may first produce a real but strictly bounded effect. Protected evidence of what actually occurred is subsequently examined by an independent validator. Only successful validation establishes the protected continuation condition required for a subsequent, potentially broader effect. The distinction is fundamental: the AI agent's assertion that an action succeeded is not proof that it happened correctly, and a receipt alone is not authorization to continue. The proposed architecture incorporates: Real-effect validation: Verification of actual outcomes rather than reliance solely on predicted behavior, proposed commands, or self-reported success. Receipt-gated continuation: Subsequent effectuation depends on protected validation of the preceding bounded effect. Independent execution authority: Separation of the AI computation environment from protected policy, credential, validation, and effectuation components. Software–hardware enforcement: Continuation conditions realized through cryptographic objects, derived or split keys, protected state, hardware latches, or equivalent mechanisms. Finality Sink verification: Independent checks at the effect-capable boundary, including act, destination, scope, phase, freshness, and revocation conditions. Taint and provenance controls: Consideration of untrusted inputs, prompt-injection exposure, credential surrogation, and privilege-separated execution. Fail-closed recovery: Explicit handling of missing receipts, uncertain outcomes, conflicting authentic evidence, validator compromise, crash recovery, and unauthorized retries. Controlled escalation: Protected human review, bounded automated remediation, reduced-scope continuation, and termination where required. The paper develops a formal protocol vocabulary, validation predicates, continuation mechanisms, six conformance profiles, implementation-invariance rules, illustrative workflows, and an analytical model of residual exposure. Potential applications include frontier AI agent infrastructure, autonomous tool execution, cloud and network operations, financial transactions, critical infrastructure, and robotic systems. The central research proposition is that AI safety should not end at the moment permission is granted. For consequential autonomous operations, the authority to proceed can be made technically dependent on independently verified evidence of what actually occurred. This publication presents a proposed architecture and analytical design, not an experimentally validated production system. It does not establish that any existing commercial platform implements the proposed mechanisms. Patent disclosure: The architecture described in this publication is identified as patent pending under Indian Patent Office application 202631117633, titled “Systems and Methods for Cryptographically Staged Effectuation with Verified Partial Effect, Receipt-Bound Full Effectuation, and Software-Hardware Enforcement.” Patentability, enforceable scope, and relationships to other technologies are not determined by this publication. Independent technical review, adversarial evaluation, implementation criticism, and discussion of related prior art are welcomed.

AI systems are increasingly common in decision-making tasks. However, these systems often generate probabilistic responses, resulting in uncertainty in their outputs. Understanding this uncertainty can help users make robust decisions, such as when to trust the agent and whether to seek more information. Interpreting uncertainty is not always straightforward, though; past work shows there is variability in how people interpret probabilistic information (e.g., weather forecasts). This study builds on that research by analyzing how people interpret probabilistic AI responses. In this survey-based experiment ( N = 632), participants interpreted AI uncertainty statements. The word used to describe the uncertainty (confidence, certainty, reliability, or accuracy) varied between trials. Participants often treated confidence and certainty as indicators of how sure the agent was about its output, whereas interpretations of reliability and accuracy were more variable. These findings can guide how AI systems communicate uncertainty, supporting more accurate user interpretations and robust decision-making.

Supervised fine-tuning (SFT) remains a widely used approach for post-training large language models, because fixed demonstrations can directly introduce desired reasoning strategies and behavioral patterns. Yet forcing a model to imitate externally provided trajectories may also interfere with behaviors already supported by pretraining, limiting generalization beyond the training distribution. Recent dynamic SFT methods mitigate this issue by reweighting token-level supervision according to model-side signals such as predictive probability, prior support, or distributional compatibility. However, model compatibility is not equivalent to learning value: a token that is weakly supported by the current model may either be an undesirable mismatch or precisely the task-specific decision that the demonstration is intended to teach. We propose CIG-SFT, an information-theoretic framework that estimates the task-conditioned information carried by each demonstrated token. Under teacher forcing, we compare the token likelihood from a frozen reference model with and without access to the task input while keeping the gold solution prefix fixed. The resulting conditional information gain quantifies how much the task itself reduces uncertainty about the demonstrated decision. We then convert this information into a KL-regularized projection of the current policy and derive an equivalent scalar-weighted SFT objective whose logit gradient exactly matches that of the projected target. Across mathematical reasoning and code-generation benchmarks, CIG-SFT consistently outperforms standard SFT and recent adaptive fine-tuning baselines, with particularly strong improvements in generalization to challenging evaluation distributions, while requiring neither additional training data nor online rollouts.

Multimodal LLMs can fail to read text embedded in an image's coarse structure (text a human recovers by squinting) and report that no text is present. We name this class Squint Text and study it as a recognition deficiency, motivated by cases from a production moderation pipeline. We introduce SquintBench, comprising 1076 production-derived moderation images, and SquintCtrl, a controlled synthetic suite for mechanism diagnosis. Frozen-weight analysis shows that hidden text leaves a coarse signal while glyph identity is weakly represented; identity becomes substantially more accessible when the correct spatial regions are supplied, implicating spatial selection as a major bottleneck. Suppressing high-frequency content also improves reading at a fixed visual-token budget, while visual token count may also contribute. These findings motivate Squint OPSD: a frozen teacher receives a downscaled view and the ground-truth transcription as privileged context, and its token-level distributions supervise a student along on-policy trajectories. At inference, the student reads the original image alone. Squint OPSD reaches 88.61 ANLS on SquintBench, versus 26.50 for the unadapted backbone, 24.44 for the best general-purpose model on the original view, and 68.60 at best for an off-the-shelf model under a downscaled view. These results substantially narrow the gap between available visual evidence and its generated read-out without auxiliary views at inference.

Studies report an elevated prevalence of endoscopy-related musculoskeletal disorders in gastroenterologists. Interventions primarily address work environment and work organization, not tool design (the endoscope). This study evaluated an add-on adjustable support strap designed to reduce the workload of the user’s left hand, which operates the endoscope’s control section. Study participants (four women, seven men) were experienced in endoscopy. Each participant performed two simulated colonoscopies with the support strap and two without (within-subjects design). Effects of the support strap were assessed using normalized muscle activity (nEMG) from surface electrodes over finger and wrist flexors and extensors and trapezius m., video, and usability data. With the strap, nEMG was reduced in most muscles for three participants (all women); mixed results for four, and no reduced nEMG for four others (all men). Mode of ratings of usability, usefulness, and desirability were 7, 5, 5, respectively (7 = very good). Results suggest benefits for some users.
topics: Occupational Health and Safety in Workplaces

documents.abstract: In September 2026, the leaders of the largest frontier AI laboratories said in public that the pace of capability improvement is too fast and that none of them can slow down alone, and agents under evaluation at OpenAI broke out of their test environment and reached a third party's live systems, which a UN-mandated panel called an early warning of one route to loss of human control. This paper examines the institutional side of that risk: not the machine, but the person who must control it. We argue that control is not taken by AI but given away, one delegation at a time, by organisations arranged so that nobody is positioned to say no, and we define control as a person who can detect a serious problem, challenge the decision, stop the system and reverse it, and who has something to lose by not doing so. Three questions follow, which any builder, funder, regulator or deployer can answer in public: (1) who inside the organisation can say no, and who answers for saying yes; (2) who outside the organisation checks the decision, and what can they do when they disagree; (3) what happens when AI builds AI faster than anyone can check it. A checkable answer needs a named person, a date, a number, and a stop that has been used or tested. Three measures meet that test: a named person on every consequential decision, including the standing instructions AI agents carry out; a supervisor with a stop authority; and two published clocks, time to build against time to check. We show that governance theory arrives at the same conditions, and code fifty older mechanisms against the questions, finding that almost every one began as one rule at one point, taken by one party without waiting for the rest. That is the paper's design: a start, not a solution. Publication is the first step and one laboratory can take it alone; the contract, the independent body and the law come after.
topics: Ethics and Social Impacts of AI

documents.abstract: This presentation examines artificial intelligence agent orchestration as an emerging security perimeter in modern multi-agent systems. It explores how increasing agent autonomy, delegation mechanisms, tool integration, and inter-agent communication introduce new cybersecurity risks and governance challenges. The presentation analyzes major orchestration architectures, including deterministic workflows, orchestrator–worker systems, agent handoffs, decentralized multi-agent configurations, and learned orchestration. Particular attention is given to the Model Context Protocol (MCP), Agent2Agent (A2A) communication, trust boundaries, access control, and security vulnerabilities arising from interactions between autonomous agents and external tools. Drawing on recent cybersecurity incidents, technical standards, and research published in 2025–2026, the presentation evaluates the effectiveness and limitations of multi-agent architectures and discusses approaches to secure orchestration, verification, accountability, and human oversight. The central argument is that cybersecurity in agentic AI systems depends not only on individual model reliability but also on the governance and security of the entire orchestration process. Presented in connection with the V International Conference “Challenges and Reality of the IT-Space: Software Engineering and Cybersecurity” (SECS-2026), October 29–30, 2026, Kyiv, Ukraine (online).

The professional kitchen demands cognitive and emotional resources from its workforce. It is characterised by time pressure, sensory intensity, and hierarchical dynamics in pursuit of perfection, creating demands on the brain. Yet professional chefs demonstrate passion, motivation, and lifelong commitment to culinary mastery. Understanding how the brain adapts to support this dedication requires integrating neuroscience and motivational psychology through neuroadaptation. This chapter explores chefs' neuro-motivational role, arguing that the brain not only engages with the culinary profession but also distinguishes high-performing chefs as wired professionals shaping identity, resilience, and creative excellence. The chapter addresses stress and resilience in the professional kitchen burnout due to anxiety, distress, long hours, and pressure. Research suggests coping strategies produce adaptive changes in stress regulation, helping chefs to maintain intrinsic motivation and resilience, with implications for culinary education, professional development, and kitchen culture.

Personal agents increasingly connect to services across the web and applications by using tools. As the effects of their actions accumulate and interact across services, unintended or harmful outcomes can arise when agents fulfill benign user requests. Proactively identifying these compositional failures requires systematically exploring diverse cross-service paths. Existing red-teaming methods often simply prompt LLMs to identify potentially harmful paths from task and environment descriptions or decompose harmful objectives specified by humans or LLMs into seemingly benign action combinations. However, generation is biased toward patterns learned during training, potentially favoring familiar tool combinations and leaving novel cross-service interactions underexplored. To address this, we propose X-AgentRed, a self-evolving red-teaming framework that discovers harmful tool call paths through a graph of tool dependencies and expands and refines them using execution feedback. By analyzing each tool's effects, potential harms, and preconditions for execution, the red-teaming agent constructs a directed graph that captures how one tool's effects can satisfy another's execution preconditions. Recipes sampled from this graph are instantiated as realistic scenarios in which agents can produce harmful outcomes. Execution feedback enables self-improvement by diversifying paths that produce harm through tool substitution and refining preconditions at blocked steps in unsuccessful paths to enable further execution. Across four frontier agentic models, X-AgentRed achieves $1.77\times$ the harmful path rate of STAC and explores a more diverse set of tools, yielding $2.99\times$ the tool coverage on average.

Enterprise AI agents now read tickets, documents, and web pages and then act on what they find through tool protocols such as the Model Context Protocol (MCP). Because an agent combines untrusted input with delegated privileges, it creates a path from attacker-influenced content to privileged action that earlier Zero Trust programs did not anticipate. This article examines how the principles of NIST SP 800-207 should be extended for agents. It compares five approaches that organizations use to give agents access to enterprise systems, from shared API keys to task-scoped delegated tokens enforced at a gateway, and evaluates them against five attack classes: indirect prompt injection, tool poisoning, confused-deputy misuse, token theft and replay, and excessive agency. An exposure analysis of a representative service-desk agent shows that task-scoped, audience-bound, sender-constrained tokens reduce exposure by about five orders of magnitude compared with a shared key, while gateway mediation constrains what a hijacked agent can do with the access that remains. The article closes with an adoption roadmap and measures of progress.

This article is for those who manage critical information systems in large enterprises and the public sector. It presents 19 principles that cannot be circumvented, a three-lines-of-defense model, practical cases on protecting the security of your systems, their owners, operators, and users, and the role of the incident manager with veto power. The material is based on 26 years of experience and has been validated in a system with 10,000+ users and 3,000+ legal entities. Who it is for. IT directors, owners, operators, and technical support operators of critical information systems, EDI product owners, heads of technical support and maintenance services, methodologists, and system ideologists. Why this matters right now. Ten to fifteen years ago, electronic document interchange was seen as a convenient add-on to paper workflows: files, folders, approval routes. Today the situation has changed fundamentally — and in several directions at once: 1. Information systems have become incomparably more complex. A modern EDI system is not a "folder with files." It is dozens of integrations: with HR systems, with the Unified State Register of Legal Entities, with electronic signature systems, with external counterparties, with mobile applications, with reporting systems. Each integration is a point where a technical action can become a legal one.2. Legislation has become more complex and stricter. Requirements for information protection are constantly growing. FSTEC orders, requirements for government information systems, personal data systems, and critical information infrastructure are not "recommendations" but mandatory norms. A regulation written five years ago may no longer comply with any current requirement — and no one will know until an inspection or an incident occurs.3. Supervision over personal data violations has become stricter. Fines under Federal Law No. 152-FZ have risen to RUB 20 million. Each identified document containing personal data in an unintended system is qualified as a separate violation.4. Electronic signatures have turned document flow into a legally significant process. Under Federal Law No. 63-FZ, an electronically signed document is equated to a paper document with a handwritten signature. This means that any administrative action with such a document — replacing a file, deleting metadata, adding a scan that differs from the signed version — is not a "correction" but potential falsification of evidence or official forgery (Articles 292, 303 of the Criminal Code of the Russian Federation).5. Artificial intelligence without principles will turn chaos into chaos squared. AI does not account for legal risks unless it has been told to. If AI is implemented in a system without described processes, unified approaches, and principles, it does not eliminate chaos — it scales it. The only way to use AI safely is to describe the principles first, and automate afterwards. What this means for EDI regulation. All five factors converge at a single point: a regulation built solely on ITIL practices, GRC requirements, and HRO principles no longer protects. It describes processes but does not answer the question of what to do if a technical action is a legal act. It assumes that principles are already established — but does not say where they come from. It describes reliability — but does not provide a structure. That is why today we need principles that stand before methodologies and beyond their scope. Principles that cannot be circumvented by an order, by urgency, or by personal agreements. Principles that protect the system before it becomes a source of legal risk.

Аннотация. Статья посвящена проблематике, включающей оценку ожиданий медицинских работников в отношении влияния ИИ-агентов на организацию медицинской помощи и выявление межсекторных различий. В исследовании для сбора эмпирических данных использован метод анкетного опроса экспертов амбулаторно-стационарного звена государственных и частных медицинских организаций. В оценках использованы 10-балльные шкалы, агрегированные в домены эффективности, нагрузки, безопасности/доверия, экономики и ИТ-готовности. В результате исследования выявлено, что во всех доменах получены значения выше нейтрального уровня, а наивысшие — по безопасности пациентов. Выявлен высокий потенциал ИИ-агентов для оптимизации клинико-административных процессов. Проведенные расчеты продемонстрировали, что статистически значимых различий между секторами не имеется, но при этом сохраняется умеренный скепсис в отношении ИТ-готовности и передачи ИИ критически важных решений. Сделан вывод о том, что ИИ-агенты обладают значительным потенциалом трансформации системы здравоохранения, однако его реализация требует взвешенного подхода, сочетающего максимальное использование технологий с ответственным управлением присущими им рисками и неопределённостями. Annotation. The article is devoted to the problematics, including the assessment of expectations of medical workers regarding the impact of AI agents on the organization of medical care and the identification of intersectoral differences. In the study, the method of questionnaire survey of experts of the outpatient-inpatient link of public and private medical organizations was used to collect empirical data. In the assessments, 10-point scales were used, aggregated into domains of efficiency, load, safety/trust, economy and IT readiness. As a result of the study, it was revealed that in all domains, values above the neutral level were obtained, and the highest — on patient safety. The study identified a high potential for AI agents to optimize clinical and administrative processes. The calculations showed that there were no statistically significant differences between the sectors, but there was still moderate skepticism about the IT readiness and transfer of critical decisions to AI. The study concluded that AI agents have significant potential to transform the healthcare system, but their implementation requires a balanced approach that combines the maximum use of technology with responsible management of the inherent risks and uncertainties.

documents.abstract: Выявлена роль объективной и согласованной оценки со стороны родителей и тренера, как фактора эффективного формирования внутренней мотивации достижений у младших школьников, занимающихся в спортивной секции карате Киокушинкай. В ходе исследования разработан и апробирован комплексный диагностический инструмент, включающий два парных опросника для родителей и тренеров, позволяющих оценить спортивную вовлечённость, психологическое благополучие и уровень поддержки ребёнка. Основные результаты показали высокий уровень мотивации у всех обследуемых, при этом статистический анализ (t-критерий Стьюдента и U-критерий Манна-Уитни) подтвердил отсутствие значимых расхождений между восприятием двух групп взрослых, что создаёт эффект «психологического резонанса». Установлено, что совпадение объективных оценок родителей и тренера обеспечивает когнитивную ясность и эмоциональную безопасность ребёнка, тогда как их расхождение порождает мотивационный вакуум и риск выученной беспомощности. Перспективы исследования включают масштабирование предложенного диагностического комплекса на другие виды спорта и возрастные группы, а также разработку программ психолого-педагогического сопровождения младших школьников при занятиях спортом. This article explores the role of objective and coordinated assessment by parents and coaches in developing intrinsic motivation for achievement in primary school students enrolled in a Kyokushinkai karate sports section.The study developed and tested a comprehensive diagnostic tool, including two paired questionnaires for parents and coaches, to assess the child's athletic involvement, psychological well-being, and level of support.The key findings revealed high levels of motivation across all subjects, while statistical analysis (Student's t-test and Mann-Whitney U-test) confirmed the absence of significant differences between the perceptions of the two groups of adults, creating a "psychological resonance" effect.It was found that convergence between objective assessments by parents and coaches ensures cognitive clarity and emotional security for the child, while discrepancies between them create a motivational vacuum and the risk of learned helplessness.Future research prospects include scaling the proposed diagnostic complex to other sports and age groups, as well as developing programs for psychological and pedagogical support for primary school students during sports activities.
topics: Martial Arts: Techniques, Psychology, and Education

Актуальность исследования определена тем, что уровень цифровой грамотности в вопросах здоровья среди медицинских сестер амбулаторно-поликлинических учреждений во всем мире варьируется он выше у тех, кто проходит целевое обучение. В исследовании проанализированы и систематизированы научные работы за 2021—2025 годы, посвященные определениям и компонентам цифровой грамотности в сфере здоровья, используемым цифровым инструментам, методам самооценки, отношению медсестер к цифровизации, а также национальным особенностям цифровой грамотности медицинских сестер. Доказано, что наиболее распространенными инструментами повышения уровня цифровизации амбулаторных клиник являются электронные медицинские карты, телемедицинские консультации, образовательные порталы для пациентов, системы удаленного мониторинга и решения на основе искусственного интеллекта. В результате проведения вторичного анализа данных выявлено, что медицинские сестры в целом положительно относятся к цифровым технологиям, но их внедрение ограничивается нехваткой времени, технических ресурсов и недостаточной интеграцией цифровых инструментов в рабочие процессы. Сделан вывод о том, что для повышения уровня цифровой зрелости и расширения перечня цифровых компетенций медицинских сестер требует целенаправленных специализированных инфраструктурных преобразований, включающих в себя организацию образовательных программ. Разработаны практические рекомендации, включающие стандартизацию оценки, интеграцию цифровых компетенций в учебные программы и применение контекстно-ориентированных подходов к обучению медицинских сестер амбулаторных клиник. Annotation. The relevance of the study is determined by the fact that the level of digital literacy in health issues among nurses in outpatient clinics around the world varies, and it is higher among those who undergo targeted training. The study analyzes and systematizes scientific works from 2021 to 2025 on the definitions and components of digital literacy in the field of health, the digital tools used, self-assessment methods, nurses' attitudes towards digitalization, and the national characteristics of digital literacy among nurses. It has been proven that the most common tools for increasing the level of digitalization in outpatient clinics are electronic medical records, telemedicine consultations, educational portals for patients, remote monitoring systems, and artificial intelligence-based solutions. A secondary data analysis revealed that nurses generally have a positive attitude towards digital technologies, but their implementation is limited by a lack of time, technical resources, and insufficient integration of digital tools into work processes. It is concluded that in order to increase the level of digital maturity and expand the list of digital competencies of nurses, it requires targeted specialized infrastructure transformations, including the organization of educational programs. Practical recommendations have been developed, including the standardization of assessment, the integration of digital competencies into educational programs, and the application of context-based approaches to training nurses in outpatient clinics.

This study examines the construct validity of LLM-based generative agents in simulating reactive, proactive, and co-occurring aggression in children. Four distinct agents were instantiated using a theory-driven parameterization grounded in the social information processing model. A total of 1,920 simulation runs were conducted across eight social scenarios, employing a hybrid blind-coding pipeline to extract 32 quantitative behavioral indicators. Results demonstrate robust discriminant validity relative to a non-aggressive baseline, with large effect sizes. High cross-seed reliability confirms that behavioral differentiation is driven by underlying psychological parameters rather than model stochasticity. Qualitative narrative analyses further converged with established empirical literature. Overall, these findings indicate that theory-parameterized LLM agents can accurately reproduce distinct aggression subtypes, offering a scalable, highly controllable framework for hypothesis generation, intervention piloting, and the refinement of psychological measurement tools.
topics: Child and Adolescent Psychosocial and Emotional Development

documents.abstract: Background The integration of Generative AI (GenAI) in higher education creates a paradox between technical efficiency and cognitive depth. Current institutional responses rely more on fragmented oversight than on ecology- and process-oriented assessment. There is a lack of diagnostic tools to map psychometric thresholds when strategic cognitive shifts transition into functional dependence. Methods We present a simulation-based methodological framework using the Tripartite Confirmatory Factor Analysis–Graded Response Model (CFA-GRM). Grounded in the cognitive-affective-conative tripartite model, this study uses a Monte Carlo simulation (N = 1,000) to demonstrate how latent interaction pathways can be structurally validated and how item parameters can be calibrated against a pre-specified diagnostic threshold ( θ ≈ 0.5), with a replication study to establish parameter recovery. Results Across 200 replications at each of N = 1,000 and N = 300, all 400 converged with admissible solutions and recovered the generating parameters with maximum absolute relative bias of 0.040; interval coverage met conventional criteria for 11 of 15 parameter groups at N = 1,000 and 8 of 15 at N = 300. In the single illustrative dataset, the fit is near-perfect (robust CFI = 0.995, RMSEA = 0.010) because the generating and estimated models coincide, a property of the design rather than evidence for the model. Test information peaks at θ ≈ 0.07–0.22, not at the proposed threshold of θ ≈ 0.5. Furthermore, we introduce a Transdisciplinary Calibration Matrix that translates these psychometric signals into context-specific pedagogical interventions across four epistemic layers, in line with SDG 4. Conclusions This study does not claim empirical generalization. It provides a methodological blueprint, a recovered parameter set, and a shared diagnostic language for future empirical work on the ethical and adaptive integration of GenAI in higher education, aligned with SDG 4.

Fourteen AI Paradoxes: A Collection of Philosophical and Algorithmic Dilemmas By Tanuj Arora (2026) This publication presents a collection of fourteen conceptual paradoxes and philosophical thought experiments exploring the inherent tensions, unintended consequences, and ethical dilemmas associated with artificial intelligence. Each paradox examines a scenario in which the pursuit of technological perfection, algorithmic efficiency, or automated intelligence creates an unexpected conflict with human values, autonomy, identity, or societal well-being. The collection encompasses questions surrounding artificial intelligence, competitive optimization, autonomous decision-making, synthetic digital ecosystems, recursive learning, predictive control, cognitive dependency, digital identity, simulated empathy, privacy, and algorithmic governance. Through fourteen distinct scenarios, the work raises a central philosophical question: Can artificial intelligence achieve its intended objectives so effectively that it ultimately undermines the very purpose for which it was created? These paradoxes are presented as conceptual explorations rather than formally established logical contradictions. Their purpose is to encourage philosophical reflection, critical discussion, and interdisciplinary inquiry into the evolving relationship between humanity and intelligent machines. The collection is intended for researchers, philosophers, technologists, AI developers, and readers interested in the ethical and existential implications of artificial intelligence.
topics: Ethics and Social Impacts of AI

documents.abstract: Puzzles are widely used to evaluate the reasoning capabilities of artificial intelligence (AI) systems for sequential decision making, yet approaches originating from different paradigms are rarely compared under unified conditions. To address this gap, we introduce a three-dimensional characterization framework that enables the analysts of AI methods by 1) projecting them to the Markov decision process (MDP) sequential decision making formalism, 2) degree of autonomy through human prior ranking of their designs and, 3) skill and computational cost. Using this framework, we analyze how representative graph-based, reinforcement learning, and large language model (LLM)-based approaches differ in their design choices and performance characteristics, instantiated respectively by Neurosolver, forward-backward reinforcement learning (FBRL), and automated thought-of-search (AutoToS), including a double-agent extension of thought-of-search (DA-ToS). The analysis relies on the Tower of Hanoi puzzle that provides a controlled benchmark with well-defined rules and scalable complexity, enabling consistent comparison across increasing problem sizes. The 3D characterization reveals that LLM-based methods, due to their weakly constrained action-space design, shift complexity from architecture to inference-time verification, leading to substantially higher memory and runtime costs than Neurosolver and FBRL.

This chapter, per the authors, introduces the Decentralized Skill Exchange Network (DSEN), a unified sociotechnical framework reconstituting peer-mediated learning on Web3 foundations. Centralized learning platforms consolidate credential authority, behavioral data, and recommendation logic within single institutional entities, producing systems that are opaque, privacy-compromising, and resistant to learner agency. DSEN integrates four architecturally interdependent components: Ethereum-compatible smart contracts on Polygon Layer-2; a FedProx-based federated recommendation engine trained on locally held device data; W3C-compliant Decentralized Identifiers and Verifiable Credentials for self-sovereign identity; and a token-governed incentive economy sustaining peer knowledge exchange without institutional intermediaries. Drawing on trustworthy federated reputation systems, Proof-of-Learning consensus, personalized federated recommender architectures, blockchain-enabled value co-creation theory, cross-chain interoperability, and FL-KG-LLM convergence research.

documents.abstract: Assume Theorem 2.3 (rigidity of wild character laws) of the OpenAI preprint The Euclidean plane is not five-colorable. We prove that, for every n ≥ 2 and every set Λ of positive real algebraic numbers, a Λ-avoiding k-colouring of Rn (with no regularity assumption) yields a conull Borel partition of Rn into k sets, each containing no two points at a distance in Λ. Consequently, conditionally on that theorem, χ(Rn) ≥ ⌈1/m1(Rn)⌉, where m1(Rn) is the supremum of the upper densities of measurable sets avoiding distance 1. With the published bound on m1(R3) (DeCorte, de Oliveira Filho and Vallentin) this gives χ(R3) ≥ 7 (previously known lower bound: 6, Nechushtan 2002). We also derive conditional consequences for unbounded and m-element sets of forbidden distances and for finitary fractional chromatic parameters, whose conditional novelty lies in dimensions 2 and 3. For n ≥ 4 and distances with rational squares, James Davies (arXiv:2610.12301) has independently proved, unconditionally and by a different method, that the chromatic and measurable chromatic numbers coincide; his theorems do not cover dimensions 2 and 3. The transfer in the plane is due to OpenAI; our contribution is its extension to higher dimensions, which is new for n = 3. Status. All main results are conditional on Theorem 2.3 of OpenAI's preprint (github.com/openai/math, item 158), which has not been refereed. The note was written with AI assistance (Claude, Anthropic), directed by the author, who is not a professional mathematician, and was checked by independent AI referee passes (OpenAI's ChatGPT and Google's Gemini). It has not yet been reviewed by a human expert. Corrections are very welcome.
topics: Limits and Structures in Graph Theory

documents.abstract: Abstract Cloud computing is a fundamental paradigm in modern computing; however, its distributed and multi-tenant nature increases exposure to cyber threats, making effective intrusion detection essential. Despite recent advances in artificial intelligence–based intrusion detection systems (IDS), many existing approaches remain sensitive to class imbalance, computationally demanding, and insufficiently robust under large-scale network traffic conditions. To address these challenges, this paper proposes an AI-driven intrusion detection framework, termed Secured Deep Generative Adversarial Rat-Optimized Diagonal Matrix (SDGA-RODM), designed for efficient intrusion detection in large-scale cloud network traffic environments. The proposed framework integrates three key components: (i) a mean divergence regularization (MDR)–based preprocessing strategy to mitigate class imbalance without altering intrinsic data distributions; (ii) a rat-optimized diagonal matrix score (RODMS)–based feature selection mechanism to derive compact and discriminative feature subsets; and (iii) a Wasserstein generative adversarial learning–based classifier (DWGALC) to enhance robustness under complex and imbalanced attack patterns. Extensive experiments conducted on the LUFlow and CIC-IDS-2017 benchmark datasets demonstrate that SDGA-RODM achieves improved performance compared with the evaluated representative IDS methods, including deep learning, ensemble-based, and optimization-driven approaches, achieving up to 6–8% improvement in detection accuracy, 15–40% reduction in classification error, and up to 30% reduction in training time under imbalanced traffic conditions. These results indicate that SDGA-RODM provides an effective and computationally efficient intrusion detection framework, demonstrating promising performance and robustness under controlled benchmark and simulation-based settings representative of cloud network traffic environments.

OBJECTIVES: To investigate the feasibility of exercise classes undertaken in the workplace during work time in healthy menopausal women, and to study the potential benefits of this intervention. STUDY DESIGN: Of the 28 women (54.3 ± 6.5 years old; 162.6 ± 7.6 cm; 65.6 ± 12.5 kg) enrolled in the study, 22 completed it. It consisted in two testing sessions before and immediately after a 12-week exercise intervention that comprised two exercise classes (a choice from body conditioning, Zumba Gold, Pilates and high-intensity interval training) and two independent exercise sessions (exercise and timing of their choice) weekly. MAIN OUTCOME MEASURES: Feasibility outcomes, including drop-out, retention and compliance, were measured during the intervention, and semi-structured interviews were conducted post-intervention. Psychological outcomes, menopause symptoms, physical activity levels and anthropometric and fitness variables were measured before and immediately after the intervention. RESULTS: Participants' drop-out, retention and compliance were 14.3%, 78.6% and 79%, respectively. The exercise programme had a positive effect in four main areas: positive organisational work culture, impact on menopausal physiological outcomes, impact on menopausal psychological outcomes, and improvements and growth for the programme. Finally, participation in the intervention was associated with favourable changes in body fat in the trunk, physical performance, menopause symptoms, mental health, and integrated and intrinsic motivation; however, the absence of a control group precludes causal inference. CONCLUSIONS: A workplace physical activity intervention during work time for menopausal women is feasible and was associated with favourable changes in several psychological and physical outcomes after 12 weeks, although the lack of a control group limits our ability to attribute these changes solely to the intervention.

Accelerating sustainable innovation is a critical mandate for emerging economies. However, the high failure rate of startups, primarily driven by inefficient founder-investor alignment and information asymmetry, remains a systemic obstacle. In Indonesia, this challenge is further exacerbated by traditional matchmaking processes that rely on social networks, often excluding high-potential Micro, Small, and Medium Enterprises (MSMEs). This study introduces and validates Artificial Intelligence Machine Learning Excellence Economy (AIMEE), a novel hybrid matchmaking framework designed to democratize access to capital and accelerate the twin transition of digitalization and sustainability. Utilizing a pilot dataset of 94 startup-investor pairs from five provinces in Java, we developed a policy-aware algorithm that integrates financial metrics with five entrepreneurial dimensions, including Sovereignty Scores based on alignment with the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs). The framework employs a lightweight neural network optimized with SMOTE (Synthetic Minority Over-sampling Technique) to address data scarcity and class imbalance. Empirical validation shows that AIMEE achieves an F1-Score of 0.83, Recall of 0.82, and ROC-AUC of 0.89, significantly outperforming traditional Random Forest baselines by 12%. The model effectively identifies patterns of potential collaboration, overcoming the limitations of rigid networking. These findings confirm that AI-driven matchmaking can serve as a robust digital infrastructure to operationalize the Asta Cita vision and SDG 9, contributing to a more inclusive, resilient, and competitive innovation ecosystem in Indonesia.
topics: Data Mining and Machine Learning Applications

documents.abstract: Agricultural productivity in developing regions is significantly affected by plant diseases and pest infestations, making early detection and timely intervention essential for improving crop yield and food security. This study proposes a multimodal context-aware AI recommendation framework that integrates maize leaf image analysis and environmental conditions to support intelligent agricultural decision-making. The framework combines a deep learning-based image classification model with weather variables, including temperature, humidity, rainfall, and solar radiation, through a multimodal fusion model for maize disease diagnosis. Based on the predicted crop condition, a context-aware recommendation engine integrates rule-based agronomic knowledge with the Qwen2.5:7B large language model to generate reliable and actionable natural-language recommendations for farmers. The generated recommendations are subsequently evaluated using Llama 3.1:8B in a blind LLM-based evaluation framework. Experiments were conducted using maize leaf images from the YEESI Lab dataset and a 61-day environmental dataset from the NASA POWER database, obtained for the geographic coordinates of Morogoro, Tanzania. Three maize conditions were considered: healthy plants, aphid infestation, and maize streak virus infection. The image-based model achieved an accuracy of 91%, while the weather-based model showed lower performance due to overlapping environmental characteristics among disease classes. The proposed multimodal fusion model achieved a classification accuracy of 94%, demonstrating the effectiveness of integrating visual and environmental information for disease diagnosis. The recommendation engine achieved an overall evaluation score of 4.80/5.00 across five quality dimensions—Safety, Technical Accuracy, Relevance, Actionability, and Clarity—indicating that the generated recommendations were agronomically consistent, context-aware, and actionable. The proposed framework provides an end-to-end AI-driven decision-support solution that integrates multimodal disease diagnosis, and context-aware recommendation for precision agriculture.

Large language models face a critical privacy utility tradeoff because training data contains personally identifiable information vulnerable to extraction attacks, while existing differential privacy methods significantly degrade model performance. This work proposes the trust-weighted and ethical gradient model, a novel privacy-preserving model that addresses challenges through three integrated mechanisms. First, trust-weighted memory employs per-sample weighting based on data sensitivity to reduce memorization of sensitive information while preserving learning signals from non-sensitive data. Second, ethical gradient masking combines per-sample clipping and Gaussian noise with sensitivity-based soft masking under a tracked ( ϵ , δ ) privacy budget, while maintaining utility. Third, the ethical boundary layer classifies and mitigates risky outputs before delivery, providing a final defense against privacy leakage. A distinctive feature of the proposed approach is the integration of computational interpretations of trustworthiness, privacy, and non-intrusion into artificial intelligence privacy systems. Extensive experiments on the Pile dataset demonstrate that trust-weighted and ethical gradient models achieve a reduction in personally identifiable information leakage while maintaining baseline utility, outperforming baseline differential privacy methods in this evaluation. The model exhibits strong resistance against membership inference, extraction attacks, and linkage attacks for privacy-preserving large language model training. The selective masking improves utility compared to uniform differential privacy under the same privacy budget.

Automated methods have been proposed to overcome the limitations of human verbal deception detection, but evidence remains fragmented across disciplines. We systematically reviewed 25 years of research (289 reports, 6,136 classification models) and meta-analyzed 3,653 models nested within 97 datasets. Pooled accuracy was 74.4% (95% CI: 71.2%-77.4%) with substantial heterogeneity. Accuracy was driven by methodological quality (ground truth, data source, class balance, evaluation procedure) more than by model complexity: the adoption of embeddings and large language models has not translated into improved predictive performance. Only 12.46% of reports used data with verifiable ground-truth, and only 23.96% of models were evaluated on independent data. The pooled accuracy aligns with meta-analyses of manual approaches, suggesting a ceiling of 70-75%, unlikely to be lifted by current research conventions.

Near the ocean surface, tropical cyclone winds change rapidly with height, but direct measurements are limited because aircraft dropsondes provide only sparse and irregular observations. Continuous wind profiles are important for understanding hurricane boundary-layer processes, improving storm-surge prediction, supporting offshore engineering, and assessing coastal hazards. In this study, we developed an artificial intelligence model that combines machine learning with physical principles to reconstruct continuous wind profiles from sparse observations. The model is designed to preserve the observed surface winds while generating realistic changes in wind speed and direction with height. Tests using more than two decades of NOAA hurricane observations show that the method accurately reproduces the vertical structure of tropical cyclone winds over a wide range of storm intensities. The framework can also extend satellite-derived surface wind measurements into three-dimensional near-surface wind fields, providing new opportunities for hurricane research, operational forecasting, and engineering applications.

Ambient artificial intelligence (AI) scribes and other electronic health record (EHR)-integrated generative AI tools are entering clinical documentation workflows because they offer measurable, if still modest, gains in documentation efficiency and clinician experience. At the same time, the medical record remains a high-consequence informatics object that supports clinical communication, continuity, documentation clarification, coding, payment, and downstream organizational reporting. As AI-generated content moves through drafting, summarization, clarification, and coding-adjacent workflows, the central challenge is no longer simply whether a model can generate fluent text, but whether health systems can preserve record integrity as documentation moves downstream. We examine this problem in United States inpatient claim-linked workflows. This Perspective proposes a prebill control plane as a candidate governance model for that problem. We describe three recurring modes of record-integrity failure that motivate it: unsupported addition, clinically meaningful loss, and propagation across encounters and systems. We then outline five operational components of a minimum viable control plane: physician-led governance and oversight, evidence visibility, change control, monitoring, and auditability. The framework is intended to support safer adoption by protecting patient safety, clinician safety, and record integrity under real-world inpatient and mid-revenue-cycle workflow pressure.
topics: Artificial Intelligence in Healthcare and Education

documents.abstract: Recent quantitative literature in mathematics education has exposed a critical empirical paradox: neither classroom management nor mastery-oriented instructional practices statistically mediate the relationship between teachers' Pedagogical Content Knowledge (PCK) and secondary student achievement. Because quantitative designs rely on standardized numerical surveys, they frequently treat the interactive classroom environment as a black box, leaving the operational mechanisms behind this statistical breakdown completely unexplained. To address this literature gap, this interpretive qualitative multi-case study investigated the lived experiences of secondary school students within the Kumasi Metropolis of Ghana to explore why traditional structural optimization fails to translate into conceptual understanding. Four distinct public Senior High School mathematics classrooms characterized by highly qualified instructors yet uneven student performance were selected as bounded cases. Data collection was thoroughly triangulated over a two-month period using non-participant classroom observations, four student focus group discussions ( n = 32 ), and four semi-structured teacher interviews. Following an inductive and deductive thematic analysis guided by Self-Determination Theory, the findings revealed that students predominantly experience classroom management as a restrictive mechanism of rigid behavioral control rather than an instructional resource. Although strict behavioral strategies successfully secure classroom silence, they create an atmosphere of intense emotional anxiety that thwarts students' basic psychological needs for autonomy and relatedness. This psychological alienation creates a severe instructional barrier where students become passive spectators who engage in superficial compliance and rote copying rather than the cognitive vulnerability required to master complex mathematical tasks. Consequently, high teacher PCK remains pedagogically locked within a teacher-centered framework because the controlling environment actively thwarts the interactive, communicative discourse necessary for internalizing knowledge. This study concludes that classroom management fails as a statistical mediator because it prioritizes structural containment over genuine cognitive engagement. Based on these findings, it is recommended that the Ministry of Education and the Ghana Education Service restructure professional development to favor autonomy-supportive management frameworks and relational, error-tolerant learning environments.

Introduction: The Human and Robotic Exploration Data Archive (HREDA) is ESA’s main repository for scientific results and metadata from exploration missions and ground-based campaigns. While it offers structured search and filtering, discovery is often hindered by complex domain terminology and database conventions, limiting accessibility. To address this, we created the HREDA Conversational Search service, a Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) assistant for natural-language queries grounded in HREDA’s content. This abstract outlines how HREDA’s relational data is transformed into a semantic knowledge base for conversational retrieval. System Architecture and Methodology: Our approach implements a Python-based ETL (Extract– Transform–Load) pipeline that synchronizes a semantic index with the HREDA “source of truth” stored in PostgreSQL. The pipeline extracts and denormalizes relational entities (e.g., investigations, teams, affiliations, sponsors, industrial partners, missions/platforms) into coherent, human-readable documents designed specifically for retrieval. The central concept is the procedural creation of “Investigation Cards”: compact narrative representations of each investigation that preserve key context (purpose, actors, campaign/mission links, and associated datasets) while remaining retrievable via semantic similarity. Each card is enriched with computed metadata such as dataset counts and mission associations, then segmented into chunks using a recursive character splitter tuned for scientific/technical text. A frequent limitation of conventional RAG systems is reduced performance on high-level aggregate questions that are not explicitly expressed in any single record (e.g., “How many studies were conducted in 2020?” or “Which countries contributed most investigations?”). To address this, we add a Summary Document generation stage. The pipeline pre-computes aggregations directly in SQL (e.g., by Year, Category, Platform, Mission, and Country) and transforms these results into short, vectorizable summary texts that can be retrieved and cited by the assistant. This design shifts aggregation from the language model to deterministic database queries, improving correctness and reproducibility. All generated content—Investigation Cards, Summary Documents, and static help material (Help Pages/FAQs)—is embedded using the Sentence Transformers all-MiniLM-L6-v2 model and stored in a pgvector-enabled PostgreSQL instance. Keeping embeddings within PostgreSQL simplifies operations, supports consistent access control, and maintains tight alignment between the semantic index and curated archival content. Conclusion: The HREDA vectorization pipeline shows how scientific archives can benefit from LLM-powered conversational search while preserving data integrity. By using denormalized investigation summaries and pre-computed statistics, it enhances both record and aggregate retrieval. Future efforts will expand citation signals and explore multi-modal embeddings for broader HRE data discovery. References:[1] LangChain AI.
